plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) to zero for capital preservation.

This plan prioritizes de-risking and reducing overall portfolio volatility.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by eliminating leveraged positions and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) to reduce overall leverage and meet mandate.
Increase QQQ exposure to 17% to balance the portfolio with broad index growth.
This approach aims for risk-first growth, blending broad market exposure with reduced leverage.
Maintain a moderate cash buffer while seeking balanced returns.
balanced.read: The balanced plan targets ~2.5%/month, aiming for growth with a focus on risk management. It reduces overall leverage and concentration, offering a more stable growth profile. Expect moderate volatility and a balanced risk-reward trade-off.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) to 6% each, leaning into high-beta growth.
Add to QQQ, bringing it to 19%, to capture broad market upside.
This plan aggressively seeks growth by utilizing leverage and concentrating in high-potential areas.
It requires strict stop discipline due to amplified risk and potential for rapid losses.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month, aiming for stretched growth by leveraging exposure. It significantly increases both upside potential and drawdown risk, with leveraged ETFs subject to decay. Expect high volatility and the potential for substantial losses if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) to zero to prioritize low drawdown.
Increase QQQI to 30% to enhance monthly distributions and income generation.
This plan focuses on parking cash for yield and steady income streams.

income.read: The income plan targets ~1%/month, prioritizing steady monthly distributions and low drawdown. It eliminates high-beta and leveraged positions for stability. While aiming for reliable income, distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
